title: Rational tangent space as the dual of the differential fibre
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ be a scheme over $K$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ be a $K$-rational point, so $f\circ x=\mathrm{id}$. Let $x_0$ be its underlying point and identify its residue field with $K$ by the structural map. Put $$M_x=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}K,x^*\Omega^1_{X/K}),$$ using the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. There is a canonical $K$-linear isomorphism $$T_{X/K,x_0}\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(M_x,K),$$ where the tangent space is the dual-number tangent space of [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], transported along the residue-field identification. This isomorphism sends the constant tangent vector $x\circ p$, for $p:\operatorname{Spec}(K[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, to the zero functional. Here the dual-number ring is [def-sc-dual-numbers]. No finite-type or smoothness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0B2D, label lemma-tangent-space-cotangent-space: T_{X/S,x} = Hom_{O_{X,x}}(Omega_{X/S,x},kappa(x)); its preceding cotangent-fibre formula, specialized to S = Spec K and a K-rational point. The tensor-Hom adjunction identifies this Hom with the K-linear dual of x^*Omega.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x_0}$, write $s:K\to A$ for the structural map, and let $c:A\to K$ be the residue map after the specified structural identification $\kappa(x_0)=K$. Thus $cs=\mathrm{id}_K$ and $\ker(c)=\mathfrak m$. By [lem-sfb-relative-differentials-stalk], $(\Omega^1_{X/K})_{x_0}\cong\Omega_{A/K}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] to $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ and this module sheaf. The stalk map of $x$ is $c$: it is a local map to the field $K$, hence factors through $A/\mathfrak m$, and its composite with $s$ is the identity. Since $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has one point, the stalk of any sheaf there is its global sections (the only neighbourhood is the whole space). The pullback formula therefore gives a canonical $K$-linear isomorphism $b:M_x\xrightarrow{\sim}V$, where $V=\Omega_{A/K}\otimes_A K$. Explicitly, for a local section $u$ of $\mathcal O_X$ near $x_0$, the global germ of $x^*(\mathrm du)$ maps under $b$ to $\mathrm d(u_{x_0})\otimes1$: this follows from the universal-derivation compatibility of the first citation and the pullback-unit germ formula of the second. Every $a\in A$ is represented by such a section, so this also specifies $b$ on the differential generators used below.

proof.text: Consider $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the morphism $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ induced by $c$. It is a closed immersion by the affine quotient criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion], since $cs=1$ makes $c$ surjective. Its image is the closed point $\mathfrak m$. The identity of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: it is finitely presented with zero generators and relations, and a lift over a first-order thickening is the given structural morphism. Apply [lem-pur-conormal-sequence-smooth-immersion] to $i$ over $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring](a), the local rings at these closed points are $A$ and $K$, with stalk map $c$. By [lem-sfb-relative-differentials-stalk], the two differential stalks in that sequence are $\Omega_{A/K}$ and $\Omega_{K/K}$. The latter is zero by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]: all its generators $\mathrm da$ vanish since every $a\in K$ comes from the base. Finally $Q\otimes_K K\cong Q$, by $u\otimes a\mapsto au$ with inverse $u\mapsto u\otimes1$. Thus the cited exact sequence reduces to $0\to Q\xrightarrow{\alpha}V\to0$, where $Q=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and $\alpha([a])=\mathrm da\otimes1$. Exactness proves $\alpha$ bijective, hence a canonical $K$-linear isomorphism. Set $h=\alpha^{-1}b:M_x\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$.

source.place: Tag 06AA, lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-smooth, applied to Spec K -> Spec A; Tag 08TE identifies the differential stalks.

proof.text: The rational-point hypothesis of [lem-sc-rational-point-tangent-derivation-identification] holds because the structural residue map $K\to\kappa(x_0)$ is the specified isomorphism. Its clause (c) gives a canonical $K$-linear isomorphism $E:T_{X/K,x_0}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_K(Q,K)$. Define $F(\theta)=E(\theta)\circ h$. Precomposition by $h$ is a linear isomorphism: its inverse is $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\circ h^{-1}$, and the two composites are identities by $hh^{-1}=1$ and $h^{-1}h=1$. Thus $F$ is the required canonical $K$-linear isomorphism. For $a\in\mathfrak m$ the first-map formula of step 2 and clauses (a)-(c) of the cited tangent identification give $F(\theta)(b^{-1}(\mathrm da\otimes1))=\ell_\theta([a])=D_\theta(a)$, where $\theta^\sharp(a)=c(a)+D_\theta(a)\epsilon$. For arbitrary $a\in A$, put $a_0=a-s(c(a))\in\mathfrak m$. The defining relations of differentials give $\mathrm da=\mathrm da_0$. Since $\theta$ is a $K$-morphism, $\theta^\sharp(s(t))=t$ for $t\in K$; additivity of its stalk map and uniqueness of dual-number coefficients give $D_\theta(a)=D_\theta(a_0)$. Hence the displayed pairing formula holds for every $a\in A$. These differential tensors generate $V$ by the generator construction in step 2, so the construction is precisely the canonical differential/coefficient pairing, without a basis choice.

proof.text: Let $\theta_0=x\circ p$ be the constant tangent vector. Its stalk homomorphism, in the coordinates of [lem-sc-rational-point-tangent-derivation-identification](a), is the composite $A\xrightarrow{c}K\hookrightarrow K[\epsilon]$: the first map is the stalk map identified in step 1, and $p$ is induced by the inclusion of constants. Consequently $\theta_0^\sharp(a)=c(a)+0\epsilon$ for every $a\in A$. Uniqueness of the epsilon coefficient in clause (a) gives $D_{\theta_0}=0$, and clause (b) gives $E(\theta_0)=\ell_{\theta_0}=0$. By the formula $F(\theta)=E(\theta)\circ h$ in step 3, $F(\theta_0)=0$, the zero functional. No finite-type, smoothness, or finite-dimensionality hypothesis was used; the computation also applies when the differential fibre is zero.
